channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: White House Urges Easing Liability to Encourage AI Disclosure
item.description: At a White House meeting on Thursday, officials from President Donald Trump’s artificial intelligence task force recommended that agencies ease their cyber liability policies in an effort to incentivize AI companies to report critical incidents.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson Says Inflation Will Determine Rate Decisions
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said inflation has become the most important measure for policymakers as they consider additional interest-rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Enda Curran

item.title: SpaceX Starship Launches on Flight Test of Reusability
item.description: SpaceX’s Starship rocket took off from the Starbase launch facility in South Texas on a flight test to bring both sections of the vehicle safely back to Earth. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Colette Kress Will Face Scrutiny at Nvidia
item.description: Nina Trentmann, senior editor at Bloomberg News, says Colette Kress is likely to become more visible as Nvidia’s interim CEO, speaking more about the company’s finances, performance and plans after Jensen Huang’s departure. She speaks with Vonnie Quinn on “The Close”. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Modine Shares Gain Most in Six Years After Samsung Buyout Talks
item.description: Modine Manufacturing Co. logged its biggest single-day gain since 2020 after Bloomberg News reported the maker of cooling systems for data centers was in talks to be acquired by Samsung Electronics Co.
item.dc:creator: David Carnevali and Ryan Gould

item.title: Morgan Stanley’s Shalett ‘Incredibly’ Bullish Despite AI Turmoil
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil and the Democrats’ midterm election victories have added to concerns about the artificial intelligence boom, but those won’t derail the main driver of the bull market: capital spending on AI infrastructure, says Morgan Stanley Wealth Management’s Lisa Shalett.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kniazhevich

item.title: Match Group Keeping AI Out of Dating
item.description: Match Group is embracing artificial intelligence across its business, but CEO Spencer Rascoff says AI agents won't be allowed to date for users on Tinder, Hinge and its other apps. Rascoff says Match wants its platforms to remain a “human-only zone,” even as the company uses AI to verify identities, improve safety and block harmful messages. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss where companies should draw the line on AI and how the technology is transforming Match Group. He also weighs ibn on Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia and why he thinks companies are ultimately bigger than any one CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FBI Said to Probe Whether Software Update Caused Mass FAA Outage
item.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation doesn’t believe the communication issue affecting air traffic control was due to a cyberattack or criminality, said a person familiar with the matter. One area of inquiry is whether the outage was caused by a software update, the person said.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: Nvidia Crisis Spurs Scrutiny of Agency That Oversees Chip Curbs
item.description: The Trump administration official who runs US export control programs was looking for marquee names for his agency’s upcoming annual conference and threw an unusual option into the mix: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland and Alicia Diaz

item.title: Blackstone’s QTS Is Cutting AI Debt Sale by More Than Half
item.description: QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is slashing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough demand from investors — and refusing to pay much higher yields.
item.dc:creator: Menghan Xiao and Emily Graffeo

item.title: Fed Sees Risks Tied to Elevated Asset Prices Partly Driven by AI
item.description: The Federal Reserve on Friday flagged potential vulnerabilities stemming from artificial intelligence and elevated asset valuations in a semi-annual report on financial stability.
item.dc:creator: Katanga Johnson

item.title: Inside Jensen Huang’s Last Hours as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Bloomberg's Ian King said that situation Jensen Huang put himself in after he had multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, gave the former Nvidia CEO 'no choice' other than the resign from the company. King said that in his final days at the company Huang tried to 'cauterize the wounds' and accept responsibility, but that it ultimately wasn't enough. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Says Speculation on New CEO Candidates Is ‘Premature’
item.description: Nvidia Corp. tamped down speculation that the company is already engaging with potential chief executive officer candidates, saying it’s still in the process of selecting a firm to find a successor to ousted leader Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Huang’s Exit Leaves Silicon Valley Unsure About AI Boom’s Future
item.description: The Nvidia chief’s ouster raises new questions about a key piece of the money machine supporting AI.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas, Shirin Ghaffary and Rachel Metz

item.title: People Have 'No Idea' How Much Nvidia Impacts Daily Life, Says Aaron Brown
item.description: Aaron Brown, founder and CEO of Lumbra, said that the average person has 'no idea' how much Nvidia impacts their lives and that it remains a messaging issue the AI industry at large needs to solve. Brown, who is a former CIA officer, said that it is hard to know exactly how the woman accused of spying on Jensen Huang came to be involved, as China is good at identifying potential resources who may have inroads with business. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Everybody’s Business: China Is Writing Its Own AI Playbook
item.description:
While US AI companies are struggling with a public image problem, Chinese attitudes towards AI are generally more positive with the government leading the charge to turn its rural and inland regions into AI-driven manufacturing hubs.
Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody’s Business podcast to discuss his factory tour of EV maker Zeekr and how China is writing its own AI story. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lutnick Under Fire as Bessent Blames Commerce for Nvidia Crisis
item.description: Denver Riggleman, CEO of RIIG Technology, said that it is 'mind boggling' that anyone would defend Jensen Huang's actions as he faces the personal, political and legal fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Riggleman, who served in Congress as a representative from Virginia, said that lawmakers who want to get real answers from both Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should call on intelligence experts to advise them on their line of questioning. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ackman on Huang's Exit, Anthropic IPO Roadshow
item.description: Bill Ackman, Pershing Square founder and CEO, says it's sad to see Jensen Huang leave Nvidia and he'll go on to do something great. Ackman also says he was impressed with the presentation given by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at the company's IPO roadshow event in New York. He speaks to Bloomberg's Isabelle Lee. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic CEO Calls Computing Power Deepest Business Dilemma
item.description: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei named sourcing computing power as one of the artificial intelligence company’s biggest challenges, in a briefing ahead of its hotly anticipated initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary and Emily Forgash

item.title: Amazon Forced Into First North American Union Pact in Canada
item.description: Hundreds of Amazon.com Inc. warehouse employees in western Canada are the company’s first North American logistics workers to be covered by a union contract after an independent arbitrator on Friday imposed terms between the online retailer and Unifor, one of the largest private-sector unions in the nation.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Soper and Thomas Seal
